posts.content:
Askari Housing Society is a residential community widely known for its essentially crime-free and highly secured environment. Located in the vicinity of the north-eastern part of Lahore, Askari is considered one of the most prestigious and luxurious housing societies that offer a modern and posh living style to its inhabitants. 

Askari is highly secured and well-developed in its sense. Society is primarily developed for the army personnel and family. Only armed forces and families can make the direct purchase and sale of their properties to the civilians. In this way, Civilians can also buy property in Askari Lahore.

This gated community has the concept of a “single entry and exit point” and it’s very unique on its own.  Initially, the society had only One Phase (Askari I ) but due to the fast-paced development and high-security measures, the society has 8 fully developed and functional phases throughout Lahore and in other major cities of Pakistan. 

Striking Features

Askari delivers up to the minute standards of living that majorly includes :

  • Prime Location 
  • Commercial Market
  • Jogging Trails
  • Physical Fitness Center
  • Mosques 
  • Cafes and Restaurants
  • Medical Facilities
  • Educational Facilities
  • Modern and Posh
  • Banks facility
  • Security Surveillance
  • 24/7 CCTV monitoring
  • Single Entry and Exit Point
  • State of the art infrastructure
  • Underground Wiring
  • Sports facility

Phases of Askari Housing Society

Askari Society has different phases with each one of them holding the prime location

 

Askari 1 Lahore 

Location : Sarfaraz Rafiqui Road – Near Sadar Bazar 

Askari 1 features sports grounds, parks, a water filtration plant, a boundary wall, mosques, and 24/7 security. This Phase includes residential flats and apartments. You can also acquire flats and apartments on a rental basis. The area sizes range from 10 marlas to 1 kanal.

Askari 2 Lahore

Location: Bridge Colony Near Sheirpao Bridge 

Askari 2 accommodates commercial, and semi-commercial markets, apartments, and flats that are available for sale and rent. The phase offers state-of-the-art amenities and an efficient security system. Askari 2 features the best schools, parks, and a friendly community environment. 

Askari 3 Lahore
Location: Main Bedian Road, opposite Fauji Foundation Hospital

Askari 3 is one of the prestigious phases of Askari Housing. It offers apartments, and flats that are available for sale and rent. The eco-friendly infrastructure, serene green environment, and the utmost level of security make askari 3 Lahore, the best place to live in. 

Askari 5 Lahore
Location: Main Ferozepur Road, near Kalma Chowk Flyover & Model Town

You can find apartments, flats, and commercial hubs in Askari 5. Askari 5 is located in one of the premium locations of Lahore The area itself is a center-business point of Lahore.  The plot sizes vary from 10 marlas to 1 Kanal, delivering state-of-the-art living standards and many amenities as well. 

Given the reputation of askari projects, investors strive not to miss any offers presented by Askari projects. 

Askari 8 Lahore
Location: Near DHA Phase – 1, Faisal Ghumman Road

The phase has many add-on perks than other phases of Askari Lahore. It has a nearby commercial market, health care center, SMC (home improvement group), a well-established commercial hub, and much more.

The plot sizes in Askari range from 10 marlas to 1 Kanal. Whereas the phase has residential apartments, and flats, available for sale and rent. Along with other striking amenities, the society offers signature Askari facilities. 

Askari 9 Lahore
Location: Zarrar Shaheed Road – Near Sadar Bazar 

This phase stretches a planned road map that includes all basic amenities including health, transport, and education, and offers all the modern amenities to its inhabitants. The phase is approachable to all DHA Phases, along with neighboring areas including Askari Mosque, Askari Bank, Badminton Court, salon spa, and other training institutes. 

Askari 10 Lahore
Location: Airport Road – Near Army Museum and Amjad Chaudhary Road

Askari 10, Lahore is a premium residential area, connected to major arteries of the city, that majorly connects Airport Road and Amjad Chaudhry Road.

The thing that makes the Askari 10 unique in every sense is that it is one of the first completely developed and well-planned communities which provides a secure and modern way of living to its residents.

Although Askari is widespread its phases in premium areas of Lahore, each sector has a few features in common including, security surveillance, mosques, commercial market, CSD market, schools, and much more. 

Askari 11 Lahore
Location: Main Bedian Road, Adjacent to DHA Phase 5

Askari 11 is primely located adjacent to DHA Phase 5, on Bedian Road, accessible from Nawaz Sharif Interchange and Kamahan-Lidher Road.

Askari Housing Society Lahore is known as one of the safest areas to live in Lahore. The area is surrounded by lush green parks, clean and serene environment. 

There are quite a few investment opportunities in Askari 11.  3, and 4 bedroom apartments and flats are available with the area of 10 Marla and 1 Kanal. You can also find multiple properties available for sale, and rent.

Which one of the above phases is the best and WHY?

Certainly, ASKARI 10 stands out from the rest phases of Askari due to its

  • Premium Location
  • Accessibility to Airport, Ring Road, and major routes
  • Huge recreational spaces
  • Nearby commercial market
  • Vast educational facilities
  • Pleasing & Disciplined Living Environment

Summing up the discussion, Askari is the best yet most secure place to invest in. Please feel free to get our no-cost assistance. For any queries, information, and suggestions, send us at Info@etihadmarketing.co.

posts.title: How to BUY PROPERTY IN LAHORE – step by step guide
posts.excerpt: Buying a property in Lahore is not always easy: it can be challenging for a first-timer to buy a property without any hassle. After all, there are so many procedures, steps, and requirements, you need to know before maki...
posts.content:
Buying a property in Lahore is not always easy: it can be challenging for a first-timer to buy a property without any hassle. After all, there are so many procedures, steps, and requirements, you need to know before making an expensive mistake. The process of buying a property in Lahore includes more than just viewing the location. You also need to review your credit and financing options, find the right real estate agent, make offers and negotiate, verify, deal finalization, verify the transfer letter, and eventually, make through the deal.

Where to start when to buy a property?

At the outset, there are certain things to consider before buying a property how much you want to spend, where you’d like to live and what certain things are of prime importance for you as a buyer. Here are a few queries to ask yourself:
  • How much property can I afford?
  • How much do I have saved for a down payment/booking?
  • Can I afford my desired neighborhood?
  • What is the current property value of the area?
  • How long will my commute take?
  • Is it within walking distance of amenities and activities?
Once you have the answers to these questions nailed down, you can follow these measurements.

Buying a property in Lahore – HEART of PAKISTAN

Lahore – a prosperous cosmopolitan, second largest city – is known for its rich art & culture, architectural and phenomenal history, where every nook, corner, building, and street is steeped in the history and has a story to tell. Being a centerpiece of Punjab, Lahore’s real state sector has got stellar repute. There are so many projects you can invest in, some are budget-friendly, like Dream Housing Society, some are costly but hold real worth. But how could you buy a property in Lahore and avoid misfortunate scams? Here are the necessary steps you need to consider for buying a property in Lahore. 1- Search before you buy Search is what saves you from making an expensive mistake. Whether it’s about buying a plot, house, or apartment – make sure you do your research. To make things seamless and hassle-free, consult a REAL real estate agent. 2-Find Actual Worth of Land Landlords grow rich in their sleep as it’s the only investment that gives fruitful returns. Before taking things ahead, make sure you get the actual value of the land. Perhaps finding the real value is a challenging task – but you can get real-time assistance from professionals, development authorities to get the right sum. 3-Have a Right Agent On your side More than 200 societies have been based in Lahore alone. With thousands of registered and the same sum of non-registered agents – finding the right agent is just like searching for a needle in a haystack. If you want everything to be smooth and seamless, you invest in a good real estate agent. Etihad Marketing is known for its exceptional real estate professionals, seamless and secure processes, and well-timed transactions. To avail of our services, visit Etihad Marketing, fill in your details on the website and let the experts handle the rest. 4-Access the property Visiting and surveying the land is crucial before getting into the deal. Make sure to view the exact property – as some people are misguided by showing them pictures of some other property and selling them a different property. Stay watchful and make sure everything is authentic. 5-Verify registry/ allotment/ transfer letter When a property is transferred to a new owner the seller and buyer have to complete the necessary paperwork to reflect the change. This documentation varies in public and private housing projects like registry, inteqaal, society allotment letter, and transfer letter.  However, it is necessary to ensure that the plot is transferred and registered with your name on the transfer list. 6-Negotiate Property Price Negotiation is the most powerful tool when making an offer on a property. The first step to negotiating is to evaluate the value of the property or the land that you are interested in buying. Often, real estate agents and property sellers are among the best negotiators. Why? The more information you have about the respective property, its area, and nitty-gritty detail, the better offer they can make. 7-Token money Token money or token amount is a small amount of money that the sellers have to pay the buyer as an assurance for the transaction. Token money varies from case to case and this step is taken after mutual consent has been established between buyer and seller. 8-Sale Agreement –  a legal binding A sale agreement is a legally binding contract that governs the purchase and sale of land or property. It’s made between buyer and sellers, it defined the terms of the transaction and the conditions under which a sale will occur, and it’s more simple than a simple transfer of ownership. Always Hold Copy of Sales Agreement When you are about to transfer the land or property under your name, make sure you ask for a copy of the sales agreement. It doesn’t seem necessary for you to ask for a copy but these documents will be helpful in the future. The copy of the sales agreement comes with important credentials such as the amount you have paid, check numbers, pay orders, or cash amount. It also contains the details of the property along with other details Once you have done with the paperwork, you can claim the respective property without any hurdle. Buying a property in Lahore comes up with great risk, however, you can take the above-mentioned steps into consideration to successfully make the deal.

posts.title: Major Reasons You Should Invest in Real Estate in 2022
posts.excerpt:
Investing your hard-earned money can be an excellent way to improve your financial status.

We have deeply jotted down some of the key benefits that will assist you to understand the advantages of why invest in real es...
posts.content:
Investing your hard-earned money can be an excellent way to improve your financial status. We have deeply jotted down some of the key benefits that will assist you to understand the advantages of why invest in real estate. Real estate is a great  investment opportunity out there because of the following reasons:

You can get full ownership of the tangible assets

You can easily diminish the risk associated with real estate by being strategic and knowing about the latest real estate market trends. In a nutshell, it is suggested to anticipate the real estate market.

You can get add-on tax relaxation on property

Real estate stability grows overtimes. Unlike any other investment opportunities such as stocks & bonds, real estate comes with long-term benefits and appreciation over time.

Full Control over your investment:

Real estate offers more controls than any available investment opportunity. You don’t have to rely on external sources to supervise your property.

Real estate is a hedge against inflation:

Real estate can be a good hedge against inflation because property values over time tend to stay on a steady high curve. It does not get affected by the economic unstable conditions.

Multiple assets class

In past, the three main asset classes have been equities (stocks), fixed income (bonds), and cash equivalent or money market instruments. Nowadays, most investment professionals include real estate multiple classes like commercial, residential, rental, raw land, and other financial derivatives,  cryptocurrencies in the asset class mix.

The real estate sector yields the highest return on investment

A return on investment (ROI) for real estate can vary a lot depending on how the property is financed, the costs involved, the rental income. If you are deciding to invest in the real estate sector, make sure to be aware of the pros and cons of this field.

Things to Consider before Invest in Real Estate in 2022

No matter how huge or the small investment you are going to make, do consider the following factors :
  • Location is everything in real estate
  • Market research is key
  • Cash flow is king
  • Portfolio Diversification
  • Credibility
  • Transparency
  • Installment Plans and Down Payments

Location is everything in real estate

Location is key to valuable real estate. Buyers often want and need close access to amenities, transportation, and routes. Whether it’s your residential plot or commercial rental property, it has a huge impact on your return on investment.

Market research is key

To make sure a property is fairly priced, a thorough real estate market analysis should always be carried out, before buying or selling. You need to understand the basic real estate terms, processes, pros, and cons of real estate investment.

Cash flow is king

Cash flow creates more opportunities. Reinvesting in real estate from an investment property into another investment is a great way to exponentially grow your financial stability.

Portfolio Diversification

A real estate is an excellent option if you want to diversify your investment. It means you can have many opportunities like commercial, residential, industrial, rental, and many classes of real estate in which you can invest. Before making any investment move, make sure to get detailed info about the real estate options so you can reap the benefits later.

Credibility

Credibility is a highly important factor before investing in any real estate sector. Always go through the credibility and records of the real estate firm. Make sure that the offered product is approved by local governing authorities. Check out the social media presence and customers reviews of the concerning company.

Transparency

The real estate industry is driven by trust, reliability, and credibility. Transparency is the core element of real estate. It ensures the truthfulness and validity of the company. Before capitalizing on any sort of real estate project, make sure that the operations and procedures of the company are transparent and authentic

Installment Plans and Down Payments

Down payment/ booking amount is initial up-front partial payment for the purchase of an expensive item such as a car or a house. An installment plan is a set number of the scheduled payments to be paid in a said number of months or years. Down payment and installment plan work proportionally. A large sum of down payment yields to a small number of installments and vice versa.

Disclaimer:

The information shared in this article is not construed as investment advice. We strongly advise our readers to always do their due research before investing in any public or private project. The laws and regulations of investment vary from region to region.

Real estate in Lahore is considered one of the most beneficial sectors to invest in. The best factor is that it leads you towards financial independence and you can enjoy a huge return on your investment. It continues to enhance your equity and wealth in no time.

The Best Way to Build Wealth

We know the numerous ways to accumulate wealth, but real estate is one of the most effective and best ways to build wealth. Having said that, making money in the real estate sector is profitable. This kind of investment requires sound guidance, methods, tactics, and determination. While investing in real estate is a proven and true method of earning, it, like any other business, comes with inherent dangers.

Real Estate in Lahore

What excites the mind is actually the long-term perks, that’s why real estate is always one of the most featured business sectors across Pakistan. Some types of real estate investments can generate cash flow more quickly. Other approaches can take a bit longer to create fluent cash returns. Depending on the level of interest, cash flow, risk threshold, and available start-up capital, real estate can be a rewarding investment.

Helping Hand Against Inflation

Unlike most other types of investments, real estate can offer an edge against inflation. That’s because as prices rise, so does the cash flow you get from the property. If property prices rise in your market, meaning you’re basically keeping pace with inflation.

Unforeseen Risk Factor

While Real estate in Lahore values does tend to rise over time, the real estate market is unpredictable—and your investment could depreciate or appreciate. Supply and demand, economy, demographics, interest rates, government policies, and unforeseen events all play a key role in real estate trends, including prices and rental rates. The idea of having an alternate income source is something that drives the attention of inventors towards the real estate sector.

Gain and Loss

Risk is always where there is an investment, it can be with a large scale shareholder or a small scale investor. In the real estate sector, investment is directly related to the risk along with the higher potential for return. Safe moves and small investments lead toward small returns. If you are not willing to take risks and want to stick to other investment vehicles that offer guaranteed income but low returns just like saving accounts, stocks, and bonds.

Regular Income and Cash Flow

Real estate in Lahore is consistent and reliable income especially rental properties for both residential and commercial. If you’re still working 8 hours job, that can mean additional cash to use toward vacations and nice-to-haves.

You can Impact Larger Community

There are many add-on benefits for the markets you invest in, too. You can help provide much-needed housing and stability for families, increase tax revenues, support the local economy, and more. The best part? The more our community flourishes, the more our assets appreciate. It’s a self-feeding circle that can really assist to build wealth and long-term financial security.

posts.content:
About DHA housing societies

Defence Housing Authority Lahore is a “nationally recognized” organization that strives to provide, the people of Pakistan, an opportunity to live the unconventional models of modern living. Fine-tuned to the latest worldwide developments in the field of Urban and Community Management, it has added splendor to our cities and communities. Focusing on the elements of strategic urban management, planning, development, and sustainability, it has successfully worked up its residential and commercial projects. The project was initiated in 1976 that governs housing and municipal services. Primarily, DHA aimed to develop housing for current and retired military personnel. It sold plots in its to civilians while a portion of total plots is allocated to armed forces officers, families of martyrs, and other employees as service. With the fast-paced development, DHA is now successfully running projects in major cities of the country, for example, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Islamabad, Bahawalpur, Quetta, Gujranwala, and Multan while opening its residential and businesses services for the general public as well.

Chairman and Governing Bodies 

DHA is one of the largest residential living hubs in Pakistan that was constitutionalized through an act in parliament and is managed by the Pakistan Army. President Lieutenant General Muhammad Abdul Aziz,HI(M) Administrator Brigadier Waheed Gul Satti, SI (M) Ex Secy DHA Col (Retd) Muhammad Shahjehan Ex IG Police Maj (Retd) Syed Ibne Hussain   Defence Housing Authority Lahore is a “nationally recognized” organization that strives to provide, the people of Pakistan, an opportunity to live the unconventional models of modern living. Fine-tuned to the latest worldwide developments in the field of Urban and Community Management, it has added splendor to our cities and communities. Focusing on the elements of strategic urban management, planning, development, and sustainability, it has successfully worked up its residential and commercial projects. The project was initiated in 1976 that governs housing and municipal services. Primarily, DHA aimed to develop housing for current and retired military personnel, now it sells most plots in its new projects to civilians while a portion of total plots is allocated to armed forces officers, families of martyrs, and other employees as service.

Location of DHA Lahore

Nearby housing societies

DHA Lahore builds upon the pure residential area. Which is far from the rush of inner Lahore. That’s why it gives you a soothing and clean breath. The following are the main housing societies and colonies near the DHA Lahore.
  • Saqib Town
  • Sultan Colony
  • Formanites Housing Society
  • Gulshan Colony
  • Askari 11
  • Eden city
  • Paragon city
  • Green city

Nearby Landmarks

  • Lahore’s biggest mall packages mall is reachable from every phase of DHA Lahore.
  • LUMS University is surrounded by DHA Lahore Phases.
  • Allama Iqbal Lahore Airport is just 15 min away from DHA Lahore.
  • Lahore Cantt Railway and Fortress mall are on 20 minutes drive

Masterplan of DHA Lahore

DHA Lahore has 11 phases in total. They have been named accordingly: Phase1, Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4, Phase 5, Phase 6, Phase 7, CBW Phase 8, EX AA phase 8, EX PV Phase 8, Phase 9 Town, Phase 9 PRISM, Phase 11 RAHBAR, Phase 12 EME. These phases are further divided into many sectors.

DHA Lahore phase 1 to DHA Lahore phase 4

DHA Phase 1, 2, 3, and 4 are fully developed phases of the DHA Lahore. These are the initial and old phases of DHA Lahore. Rates of plots and houses are a little higher than other phases of the region due to leverages and facilities offered by these developed phases of DHA Lahore. DHA Lahore phases 1 to 4 plots are not available on installments and payment plants but reselling of plots and houses are still in demand. Possession of land is immediate in paying all the dues. Roads and streets are at least 40 feet wide. Here developers of phases have installed their own electricity system to avoid load shedding. Overhead electricity cabling is applied in DHA Phase 1 to 4. All of these phases are in an excellent location with close proximity to all facilities and amenities. Every Sector in these DHA phases has its own Jamia Mosque and parks with playgrounds and jogging tracks. National and International Brands, Restaurants, Bars, Cafes, Banks, hypermarts, spas, and salons are located in every phase of DHA Lahore.

Location of DHA Lahore phases 1, 2, 3, 4

DHA Phase 1 Connected to many main areas of Lahore like Defence Chowk, RA Bazar, Jinnah Flyover, Nishat Colony, etc. It also serves as the connected area to other initial Phases of DHA Lahore for example DHA Phase 2, DHA Phase 3, and DHA Phase 5. DHA Phase 2 Starts from Ghazi Road which is also called Airport Road. The Main Boulevard of DHA Lahore also touches DHA Lahore Phase 2. DHA Phase 3 is accessible from two main boulevards of Lahore, Walton Road, and Ferozpur Road Lahore. DHA Phase 4 is directly accessible from Defense Road, Ring Road Lahore, and DHA Phase 5.  

Sectors of DHA phases 1, 2, 3, 4

DHA Phase 1  14 sectors named as sector A, sector B, sector C, sector D, sector E, sector F, sector G, sector H, sector J, sector K, sector L, sector M, sector N, and sector P which are completely developed. DHA Phase 2 6 sectors were named as sector Q, sector R, sector S, sector T, sector U, sector V DHA Phase 3 5 sectors were named sector W, sector X, sector k XX, sector Y, and sector Z. DHA Phase 4 9 sectors were named as sector AA, sector BB, sector CC, sector DD, sector EE, sector FF, sector GG, sector HH, and sector JJ.

posts.excerpt: Lahore smart city is beginning a new era of technology in Pakistan’s territory. The concept of smart cities in Pakistan seems to offer vast avenues for investment. Considering the comprehensive approach that is expected...
posts.content:
Lahore smart city is beginning a new era of technology in Pakistan’s territory. The concept of smart cities in Pakistan seems to offer vast avenues for investment. Considering the comprehensive approach that is expected to be adopted in the planning and development, early investors in these projects can look forward to healthy gains in the medium to long term. Since smart cities have only recently started gaining huge attraction, property investors have been in a constant dilemma of whether they should invest in them. However, land prices in and around the locations of the proposed project would witness a surge.

Deliverables of smart city 

The idea from the surface is to transform and develop cities with urban centers and class-apart infrastructure by harnessing the best of technology, architectural planning, and sustainability. Smart cities are designed to deliver quality services and experiences to their valuable investors and residents. The use of renewable resources for efficient energy systems, water recycling, and purification systems, sewerage, and waste management systems, smart building systems, security and infrastructure, traffic control systems, and much more to evolve; would be adopted across these cities. As a result, industries and companies associated with it provide such technologies that can expect an increase in investment thereby making them a good return on investment as well.

What Makes Smart Cities Fit for the Investors?

Evolving in smart infrastructure and economical living will be the prime goal of smart cities. While the mission remains to create inclusive yet urbanized spaces for communities, that comes down to the question of property investors. This article takes you through various prospects of why smart cities are investor-friendly for you to make a wise and timely investment decision. The intelligent, development-oriented approach to cities has increased the proportion of the real estate market. The exposure to smart investment, planning, and development has proven the smart cities mission to be the most remarkable driver for the growth of the real estate industry in Pakistan. There are countless reasons for property investors to invest in Lahore Smart City, and some of them are listed below.

Blossoming Real Estate Markets

Making smart cities, especially in the populous cities like Lahore will not only carter the standard of living but also come up with endless job opportunities. This effective transformation can streamline the manual process and give employees greater opportunities to reach their full potential while providing citizens with enhanced services. Recently, real estate prices have skyrocketed as investors are seeking better infrastructure, quick access to all amenities, and lower costs yet higher standards of living. Real estate agents and property investors have leaned towards the well-established standards, knowing the potential profit they can yield on their valuable investment.

Technology-Driven Living

Smart cities, as the word suggests, are technology-driven. They strive to adapt technology-enabled activities, which seek to provide a world full of resources and opportunities in itself. The main features of such cities include smart metering, an abundance of parking spaces, 24/7 surveillance, a well-managed traffic system, an eco-friendly environment, an uninterrupted supply of water and electricity, and the list goes on. All of this is enabled by the latest technological interventions making these Lahore Smart City – a sustainable and attainable solution for the future. Tech-driven involvement has boosted the confidence of real estate agents and property investors in smart cities. This is bound to increase shortly.

Infrastructural Evolution

A revolution can be witnessed in smart cities’ infrastructure due to the investment in locality-based procurement of resources. The implementation of infrastructural plans has transcended the expectations of investors and customers, making it an entirely new gigantic experience. Infrastructure forms the foundation of any smart city, and realizing the same; the government has invested heavily in it, widening the prospects of interventions and investments from property investors around the globe. All of these developments can be witnessed first-hand in the Capital (Islamabad) and the city of gardens (Lahore). Smart cities are best for long-term investment because of their probability of better infrastructure and increasing housing demand.

Improved Access to Amenities and Facilities

Another significant advantage of investing in a Lahore Smart City is accessibility to residents. posts.content:
Real estate – a term we are well aware of – is a passive income generator. But getting straight into it might come up with some unwelcomed hurdles. It’s important to know the most commonly used real estate terms used by industry professionals, developers, real state agents, and government officials who document property transactions. In particular, understanding real estate terms used in Pakistan can be complicated for beginners. Therefore, Etihad Marketing has summed up the ultimate real estate glossary for your ease that explains some of the most common property terms in Pakistan simply and understandably.

Common Real Estate Terms In Pakistan

Knowledge of the listed above are the terms commonly used in the Pakistani real estate market. It would benefit you while dealing with property matters in Pakistan.

OFFICIALS AND DOCUMENTS

AKS SHAJRA (Shajrah)

Aks-Shajra (a copy of shajra) is an image of a specific piece of land drafted on a drawing paper for individual property owners. Aks Shajra provides information about the land that has the property’s owner with their khasra numbers marked and boundaries specified. It is developed on the demand of property owners. Aks Shajra is particularly needed in dealings concerned with agricultural land.

SHAJRAH

Shajra is a detailed map that is used for legal (land ownership) and administrative purpose. It includes details like Khasra number, measurements, location, and the surrounding area. This detailed map is called SHAJRAH.

FARD (Fard e Malkiat)

Fard Malkiat is also known as (proof of property ownership, Record of Rights/ Jama Bandi/Misal Haquiat/Register Haqdaran-e-Zameen) maintained for the record of the property. This document is essential for the registration of property (registry). Fard includes comprehensive details about the property like- exact location, size, and property type. It is issued under different conditions as per the demand of the property owner, like selling, preparing general power of attorney, or for recording purposes.

GARDAVARI

Gardavri is written proof of the land-leasing rights, issued by GARDORI to the person who owns the land on lease with the owner’s permission.

GARDAVAR

Gardavar is a person, also called Qanoon-go or Kano-go, whose job is to examine the land record.

REGISTRY

A registry is documented proof of ownership of property. The process ensures that property ownership, property possession, and other rights are legally recorded with the government. This document ensures the ownership and negates any illegal transfer.

PROCESS

JAMABANDI (Fard or Parcha)

JAMABANDI is the most crucial document of revenue record. Generally, the land records are updated – every after four years. This process is known as JAMABANDI. It includes all the necessary information about ownership, the location, land type, and land division if any.

INTEQAL

The property transfer (also called inteqal) is used to transfer from seller to buyer. Inteqal is carried out based on the registry of the property.

PARTAL

Partal is the process of updating and verifying a property’s record. Partal is overseen by a patwari. The Patwaar Khana or the revenue department maintains the transfer of records.

LAND MEASUREMENTS

Acre

An acre of any land refers to an area of 8 Kanal of area. 43560 sq. ft. It is also equivalent to 160 Marlas.

Bigha

Bigha is the measurement of land equal to 4.958677686 Kanals. Bigha comprises 99.1736 Marla.

Kanal

A Kanal is equivalent to approximately 4500 sq. ft. of land. A Kanal is comprises of 20 marlas.

Marla

The measurement of marla varies from region to region. The Marla of Punjab ranges from 225 sq. ft to 272 sq. ft of land.

Moza

Moza is an area specified for the use of work or office of a revenue collector.

Sarsahi

Sarsahi is the smallest unit of measuring land. It is equivalent to 25 square feet. The real estate industry in Pakistan follows a very traditional approach, but now the advent of digital systemization of the process and records have streamlined the procedure of land maintenance and record. And Smart city is a city or municipality that is equipped with basic infrastructure to deliver a better quality of life, and a clean and sustainable atmosphere through the implementation of smart solutions in the economy, mobility, technology, energy, infrastructure, environment, people, and government. The impact of this activity can include: (1) improving the city’s efficiency of service delivery (2) enhancing the quality of life for everyone (3) increasing equity and prosperity for well being (4) valuing citizen participation

Smart City initiative in Pakistan

posts.content:
Are you ready to buy a property in Lahore? Buying a property is one of the most significant financial decisions you’ll make in your lifetime. There are, after all, a lot of things to consider. You need to figure out prices and the authentication/verification of the plot you are investing in.

You are always intended to buy legal property that is duly approved by the legal authorities.

Lahore Development Authority (LDA) has published a thorough checklist of the things you must figure out before selling or buying property in Lahore. The details along with the explanation are mentioned below. By carrying it out, you can invest in any type of housing scheme.

Investigate housing scheme

Don’t get distracted by the flashy advertisements, attractive booking offices, and inspiring brochures that get in your head. Take some time and search the housing scheme approval or authentications.

Take a trip, explore the location

LOCATION MATTERS ALOT-  Always visit the location of your housing scheme and perform a thorough survey. You’ll want to be sure that your property has easy access to your work.

Verify development or hidden charges

In the majority of the real estate advertisements, development charges are not mentioned. To avoid additional charges surprise later, obtain a written detail of total development (inclusive or exclusive) charges before making the final purchase.

Confirm utility service availability

Confirm the availability of electricity, gas, water, landline, and sewerage utilities.

Check out the amenities

Amenities vary from society to society. It also varies to the nature of the property you are about to buy. The best approach is to take an on-site visit to make sure that you are receiving the said perks of your worthy investment.

Additional Cost

Assure before the purchase that there are no additional charges, fees, and dues at any point in the future except those which are mentioned in the project administration written form.

Make Payment through Bank Draft

The best approach for any sort of property purchase and selling is to make through bank draft and save the receipt. Moreover, keep a record of the address and phone numbers of the housing scheme and its legal authorities.

Required Documents to check before buying plots

Lahore Development Authority LDA checklist also notes certain documents and issues that must be double-checked before buying plots in Lahore – details are as follows:
  • An approval letter NOC (no objection certificate) from the relevant authority
  • An approved map for the housing scheme
  • Total number of plots in the housing scheme along with the number of plots in each category
  • Details, along with plot number and block of the 20% plots within the project. 20% of the plots within a housing scheme have to be mortgaged with LDA, consistent with standard management procedures
  • Whether or not followed your plot is among LDA’s mortgage category
  • Is your plot listed on the approved map? Is it located on approved land?
  • Make sure that your plot is not situated within the area reserved for amenities plots e.g. masjids, schools, graveyards, community centers, and hospitals.
  • Ensure that the housing scheme is not accused of any kind of fraud or there are no cases registered against the housing scheme in any court of law

posts.content:
Property value is a flexible term that is influenced by a variety of situations. Understanding the primary components that might cause property value to fall is critical for making informed decisions, whether you are a homeowner, buyer, or investment. In this post, we'll look at the numerous variables that can cause a drop in property value. By learning about these characteristics, you will be better ready to navigate the real estate market with confidence. Let's examine each of these parts. In this blog we’ll discuss.
  • Factors that reduce property value 
  • Factors that influence property value

Factors that Reduce Property Value

Economic Downturn: 

Local and national economic situations might have an impact on property values.  Economic downturns can harm property values. Job losses, rising crime rates, and decreased economic activity can all lead to a decrease in demand for homes, lowering their value.

Environmental Dangers:

Property values are likely to fall in locations prone to catastrophic events or environmental hazards, such as flood zones or earthquake-prone areas, due to increased risk and insurance costs.

Deteriorating Surroundings: 

The neighborhood in which a property is located can have an important effect on its value. Because of the desire factor, properties in safe, attractive, and well-maintained neighborhoods tend to have greater values. A declining neighborhood, characterized by abandoned houses, higher crime rates, and a lack of critical facilities, can result in lower property values.

Poorly Maintained Property: 

The state of a property is very important in determining its worth. Property values tend to be greater in well-maintained properties with modern amenities and recent renovations. Regular upkeep and appropriate upgrades can help to maintain or increase property value. Neglected properties with evident indications of wear and tear, such as peeling paint, fractured foundations, or leaky roofs, are likely to be valued lower since they may require costly repairs.

Considerations for the Environment and Safety:

Properties located in areas prone to natural disasters, environmental risks, or high crime rates may lose value. Environmental concerns might result in increased insurance prices and a smaller pool of possible buyers.

Negative Market Trends:

Property values can be influenced by changing population trends. Staying up to date on market trends can assist property owners in making strategic decisions. The real estate market is dynamic, and property values fluctuate in response to market movements. Property values tend to rise in a seller's market, where demand exceeds supply, giving sellers an edge. Property values may fall during a buyer's market with low demand and abundant inventory.

An In-Depth Examination of the Factors Influencing Property Value: 

In this section, we will look deeper into the many elements that determine property value.

Property Value is Affected by Location:

Properties in desirable neighborhoods or places undergoing growth and development tend to command greater prices. The location of a property has a considerable impact on its value. A property's value can vary greatly depending on its accessibility to vital services such as schools, hospitals, public transportation, and recreational places.

Infrastructure Improvement:

New infrastructure, such as highways, public transportation networks, and commercial centres, can increase property values in neighbouring communities. Buyers are drawn to improved accessibility and convenience, which leads to increased demand and higher property values.

Interest Rates Today:

Loan interest rates can have a substantial impact on property values. Lower borrowing rates often attract more buyers, pushing up demand and property values.

Policies and Regulations of the Government:

Changes in government policy, such as tax breaks or zoning laws, can have an impact on property values. Property owners must understand these policies to make educated judgments.

Conclusion

A variety of variables influence property value, which might cause it to fall. Property owners, investors, and buyers must understand the elements that influence property value. Numerous factors influence property value variations, ranging from an ideal location and quality renovations to economic situations and neighbourhood appeal. Individuals can better navigate the real estate market and maximize the value of their houses by being knowledgeable about these aspects and making informed decisions.

FAQs

1. What are some of the outside factors that affect property value?

The neighbourhood, economic conditions, infrastructure development, environmental risks, interest rates, and government policies are all external elements that influence property value.

2. What effect does a property's condition have on its value?

The state of a property has a direct impact on its value. Property values tend to be greater in well-maintained properties with modern facilities, whereas properties in need of repairs may be valued lower.

3. Can economic issues affect property values?

Economic factors such as economic growth, job opportunities, and overall stability can all affect property values.

4. What are the most important things that influence property value?

Prime location, excellent renovations, curb appeal, good market trends, infrastructure development, and proximity to high-quality schools are the top characteristics that raise property value.

5. Can economic issues have an effect on property values?

Economic factors such as economic growth, job opportunities, and overall stability can all have an impact on property values.

6. What effect do market trends have on property value?

Property values can fluctuate according to market patterns such as a seller's or buyer's market. Property values can rise when there is a strong demand and a low supply, but they can fall when there is a low demand and a high inventory.

7. What are the hazards of investing in properties in high-crime areas?

Properties in high-crime regions are less appealing, resulting in lower property values and potential safety issues for occupants.   Are you finding this content useful? posts.content:
When navigating the world of real estate transactions, it is critical to work with a licensed professional, known as a real estate agent. These individuals operate as mediators, representing either the vendor or the buyer during the transaction. Acting on behalf of the seller, their primary goal is to obtain the greatest possible price for the property for sale. While real estate agents can help purchasers, it's crucial to remember that their ultimate allegiance is with the seller, who compensates them with a commission that is usually determined as a percentage of the final transaction price. Buyers should exercise caution and seek independent counsel to ensure their interests are appropriately protected. Understanding the Worth of a Real Estate Advisor for Property Investors is paramount in making informed decisions and maximizing investment potential.
 

Select the Best Property Investment Advisor:

When it comes to property investment, selecting the correct counsel can make or break your success. posts.content:
Real estate has become Pakistan's largest and most successful industry. With a booming real estate industry, the number of popular real estate scams in Pakistan is expanding by the day. To avoid property scams in Pakistan, you must do a real estate market analysis before investing. Proper research will save you money by preventing property fraud. Real estate scamming is a serious issue that should not be overlooked because it can cost you your hard-earned money if you buy homes with scammers. Scams are difficult to detect for ordinary people. As a result, we'll go over frequent property-buying frauds to help you prevent property scams. Here are some Common Property Scams / Frauds you need to Avoid.
 
 
Understanding the tactics used by scammers is crucial in protecting your investments. Always verify property ownership and legal documents before proceeding with any transaction. Take caution when dealing with offers that seem too good to be true, as they often are. Vigilance and due diligence are your best defenses against falling prey to property scams.
 
 

Unveiling Most Common Property Scams / Frauds:

 

False Development Update:

For the benefit of possible purchasers, the realtors also pretend to be in the process of developing a property. Instead of focusing on major infrastructure like electricity, water connections, and sewage systems, they build the main gate, boundary walls, and roads in an attempt to convince investors and end users that the development is proceeding as planned.
 

Fake Real Estate Advertising:

In order to sell their properties as quickly as possible, builders engage in fictitious marketing, which is a Common Property Scam/Fraud you need to Avoid. They provide amenities, services, and attractive savings together with simulated area views.
 

Selling Property to Multiple Customers: 

Developers and real estate agents continue to market a single property to several purchasers despite various misleading tactics, like faking official records. As a result, buying a property that is already held by someone results in financial loss for the buyer.
   

Considerations for Property Purchase:

 

Review the Title Documents:

The first and most crucial step in avoiding real estate fraud in Pakistan is to review the title documents for the property you are interested in. The title documents must be valid, and you should verify them with the appropriate authorities. Check the property's title, status, and any outstanding debts or liabilities.
 

Verify the Seller's Identity:

Make sure you know who is selling before you purchase any real estate. Their National Identity Card (NIC) is available upon request, and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) can confirm it. Additionally, you can get their tax registration number and have the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) confirm it.
 

Confirm the Property's Location:

Make sure the property is in a secure and safe place, free from Common Property Scams / Frauds You Need To Avoid, by checking its location. To make sure the property is in a safe place, you might look up the area's crime rate and speak with the local authorities.
 

Claim the Original Documents for the Property: 

A further form of fraud is when builders and real estate brokers give buyers fake property documentation. A lot of buyers invest without requesting the property's original paperwork. Thus, constantly demand your right to the property's original documentation. 
 

Employ a Real Estate Agent:

When purchasing or selling real estate in Pakistan, it is imperative to work with a reputable and trustworthy real estate agent. A qualified agent can guide you through the purchasing or selling process and help you avoid fraud. It is advisable to examine the agent's qualifications and confirm that they are registered with the appropriate authorities.
 

Use a Trustworthy Lawyer:

An additional crucial measure to avoid real estate fraud in Pakistan is to work with a reputable lawyer. A competent attorney can assist you in checking the legality of the purchase, examining the title paperwork, and confirming the seller's identification. It is advisable that you work with a real estate attorney who has handled transactions involving properties.
 

Never Pay Cash:

When dealing with real estate transactions, it's crucial to be vigilant against potential scams and frauds. Common Property Scams/Frauds You Need To Avoid include cash payments, which can pose significant risks such as fraud and money laundering. To safeguard yourself, it's advisable to refrain from making cash payments. Instead, opt for safer alternatives like using a bank draft or a check for transactions. Additionally, always ensure you obtain a proper receipt for any payment made to maintain a clear record of the transaction. By exercising caution and following these precautions, you can help mitigate the risks associated with real estate transactions.
 

Check for the Genuine NOC:

In Pakistan, there are numerous housing organizations that lack official registration. Because the builders exhibit the NOC of permitted property and assign plots to clients on the unapproved land, many individuals get trapped as a result of the excellent promotion of illegal societies.
 

Be Cautious of Unusual Discounts:

Be cautious of unusual discounts as it could be a sign of fraud if a vendor gives you an unusually large discount or an exceptionally low price for a property. Deals that look too good to be true should always be avoided, and before making any judgments, always conduct thorough research. It's crucial to stay informed about Common Property Scams / Frauds You Need To Avoid to protect yourself from potential risks.
   

Actions Need to be Done to Prevent Scams: 

 
  • Instead of seeking advice from a new realtor, investigate your agent, the property, and his reputation on your own.
  • Examine the real estate company's portfolio.
  • Examine the company's and the realtors' websites and social media pages.
  • Request a license and register the website for property marketing.
  • Don't pay huge sums of money upfront.
  • Use safe payment options at all times, such as bank transfers or approved payment networks.
  • Go to the real estate marketing company's office in person.
   

Conclusion:

In conclusion, it's critical to take precautions against real estate fraud while purchasing or selling property in Pakistan because it's a significant problem. What is a Sale Deed in Pakistan?

The Sale Deed is a title document in a sale transaction that is comprehensive, solemn, and technical, and parties normally have it written, executed, and registered with qualified legal counsel.
 

Is there a tax on selling property in Pakistan?

When you sell a house, you must pay CGT. Rates vary according to how long you've owned the property. Plots/files, for example, are taxed at 15% if sold within a year, 2.5% after 5 years, and exempt after 6. Similar requirements apply to residential and high-rise properties.
 

What is the property transfer tax in Pakistan?

In Pakistan, filers must pay a 3% tax when purchasing or transferring property, while non-filers must pay a 7-10.5% advance withholding tax.

Factors that Reduce Property Value:

 

Economic Downturn: 

Local and national economic situations might have an impact on property values.  Economic downturns can harm property values. Job losses, rising crime rates, and decreased economic activity can all lead to a decrease in demand for homes, lowering their value.
 

Environmental Dangers:

Property values are likely to fall in locations prone to catastrophic events or environmental hazards, such as flood zones or earthquake-prone areas, due to increased risk and insurance costs. Causes of Decrease in Property Value include poor maintenance, economic downturns, and changes in neighborhood demographics.
 

Deteriorating Surroundings: 

The neighborhood in which a property is located can have an important effect on its value. Because of the desire factor, properties in safe, attractive, and well-maintained neighborhoods tend to have greater values. A declining neighborhood, characterized by abandoned houses, higher crime rates, and a lack of critical facilities, can result in lower property values.
 

Poorly Maintained Property: 

The state of a property is very important in determining its worth. Property values tend to be greater in well-maintained properties with modern amenities and recent renovations. Regular upkeep and appropriate upgrades can help to maintain or increase property value. Neglected properties with evident indications of wear and tear, such as peeling paint, fractured foundations, or leaky roofs, are likely to be valued lower since they may require costly repairs.
 

Considerations for the Environment and Safety:

Negative Market Trends:

Property values can be influenced by changing population trends. Staying up to date on market trends can assist property owners in making strategic decisions. The real estate market is dynamic, and property values fluctuate in response to market movements. Property values tend to rise in a seller's market, where demand exceeds supply, giving sellers an edge. Property values may fall during a buyer's market with low demand and abundant inventory.
   

Factors that Influencing Property Value:

posts.content:
Investing in real estate is a big move that comes with both enthusiasm and responsibility. Understanding the property registration procedure in Pakistan is critical for ensuring a smooth and legally sound transaction, whether you are a first-time home buyer or a seasoned investor. It involves various steps such as verifying the ownership documents, obtaining a no-objection certificate, and completing the registration process at the relevant government office.
 
Additionally, it's essential to stay updated with any changes in property laws and regulations to avoid any legal complications in the future. A thorough understanding of these procedures not only safeguards your investment but also provides peace of mind throughout the buying process. This blog will walk you through every detail of the Pakistani property registration process, from its significance to its step-by-step approach, ensuring you have a Complete Guide on Property Registration in Pakistan.
 

Why is the Property Registration Process Important in Pakistan?

 
It's super important for making sure that the person who owns a property is officially recognized and that any deals made are totally legal. But it's not just about following the law - registering property also helps cities plan and grow better by keeping track of who owns what land. Plus, it makes real estate transactions fairer and more open, which makes investors feel safer. Especially, when there's a problem or argument about who owns what, property registration steps in to help sort things out fairly and according to the rules. Here are some of the reasons why understanding the Complete Guide on Property Registration Process is essential for all property owners:
 

Obtaining Legal Ownership:

Property registration is the official method of obtaining legal property ownership. It gives you formal confirmation that you are the lawful owner of the property, which is necessary for future transaction and legal security. 
 

Ability to Sell and Transfer:

When you register your property, you gain the legal right to sell, lease or transfer it. Without proper registration, any property transaction may be called into question, resulting in issues and dispute resolution. 
 

Protection against Frauds:

Property registration functions as an obstacle to fraudulent activity. It protects you from illegal occupation, falsified sales and claims made by those who may contest your ownership. 
 

Dispute Resolution:

Disputing your property minimizes the possibility of ownership conflicts. Conflicts with other claims are greatly reduced when ownership is established by registration.
 

Transaction Security:

The registration process establishes an official record of the transaction, including the purchase price. This record can be used as significant evidence as an event of any future legal concerns. 
 

Documents Required in Pakistan for Property Registration:

 
Certain documents are required to meet the legal requirements for property registration in Pakistan. The Board of Revenue has produced a detailed list of documents required for property registration in Pakistan to help with the process. With these documents, proof of identity such as a national identity card or passport is essential.
 
Furthermore, documentation related to property taxes and any outstanding dues may also be required by the authorities for a smooth registration process. It's important to ensure all necessary paperwork is in order to avoid delays or complications during the registration process. For a comprehensive understanding, refer to the Complete Guide on Property Registration Process,  below are the documents required for successful registration.
 

Step 1: Purchase Agreement 

The sale deed is a basic document that transfers the ownership from the seller to the buyer. It outlines the sale’s terms and conditions, property data, and the agreed-upon sale consideration. 
 

Step 2: Make a copy of your CNIC

A copy of CNIC is obtained for all parties involved. This document serves as a form of identification and establishes the legal identities of the parties. 
 

Step 3: Certificate of Mutation

The mutation certificate confirms that ownership has changed in the land revenue records. It is critical for updating ownership information and maintaining accurate records.
 

Step 4: Obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC). 

To ensure that there are no legal objections or conflicts over the property, an NOC from the appropriate governing body is required. This certificate certifies that the property is freely transferable.
 

Step 5: Certificate of Obligations: 

The encumbrance certificate verifies the property's free title, demonstrating that there are no outstanding loans, encumbrances, or claims against it. It assures that the buyer has a clear title.
 

Step 6: Power of Attorney (If applicable):

To appoint someone to act on your behalf throughout the registration process, you must have a valid power of attorney document. This document delegated authority to the selected person to represent you in the transaction.
 

Step 7: Affidavit

An affidavit is a legally binding declaration signed by the parties involved that confirms the correctness of the information presented and asserts their legal claims to the property. These documents ensure the reliability and transparency of the property registration process as a whole. By supplying these necessary documents, you help to ensure a smooth and secure property transaction that protects the rights of all parties involved.
 

Scams at Pakistan's Property Registry:

Recently, there's been a rise in scams at Pakistan's property registry, causing concerns. These scams usually include fake papers, fake signatures, and dishonest practices, which weaken the trust in property ownership. They not only threaten property rights but also shake confidence in the real estate sector. Urgent action is needed to tackle these problems and rebuild trust in the registry system. A Complete Guide on Property Registration Process would aid in addressing these issues effectively. Following are some common property registration frauds in Pakistan: 
 

Scam of Fake Documents:

The sale of stolen or fake documents is one of the most common frauds. Scammers falsify or invalidate fake title deeds, sale agreements, or other legal documents that appear real. Unsuspecting customers may be duped into believing they are buying legal property, only to discover later that their ownership is not legally recognized.
 

Multiple Claimants for Ownership:

Property with multiple ownership claims can also be a source of fraud. Fraudsters may sell the same property to many buyers, each believing they are the lawful owner. This can result in court fights, disagreements, and significant financial losses for all parties involved.
 

Unethical Agents and Brokers:

Not all real estate agents and brokers are trustworthy. Some agents may engage in unethical behavior, such as charging high commissions, misrepresenting property prices, or concealing critical information from buyers and sellers. These strategies can cause financial injury to buyers and sellers, as well as harm to the property industry's reputation.
 

Boundary Disagreements:

Scammers may modify property boundaries or generate fake documents to make a property appear larger than it is. Buyers who depend on misleading information risk receiving less property than intended or becoming involved in boundary disputes.
 

Identity Theft:

Scammers might pretend to be property owners or authorized agents to cheat people into transferring property illegally. Fake power of attorney documents or identity theft might result in the illegal transfer of property ownership. Vigilance and verifying documents thoroughly can reduce the risk of falling victim to such schemes. Always ensure authenticity before proceeding with any property transactions.
 

Work with Reputed Professionals: 

Working with reputed professionals ensures access to high-quality expertise, fostering an environment of excellence and innovation. Their proven track record and credibility infuse confidence, leading to smoother collaborations and better outcomes. Leveraging their experience and networks can significantly elevate the standards of work, ultimately driving success and recognition in the industry.
 

Pay a Visit to the Property: 

When considering a property investment, nothing beats the firsthand experience of paying a visit. Walking through the space allows for a deeper understanding of its layout, condition, and potential. It's an invaluable step in making an informed decision and visualizing the property's possibilities.
 

Use Registered Agents: 

To reduce the threat of fraud, it is essential to engage agents who are officially registered with the relevant authorities. Registration ensures conformity to regulatory standards and offers a layer of accountability, enhancing trust and minimizing the likelihood of misleading activities. Choosing registered agents helps safeguard against potential financial and legal risks associated with unauthorized or deceptive practices. Moreover, you may easily manage the property registry procedure in Pakistan by being educated and taking care of, protecting your money, and avoiding any scams.
 

Conclusion

In Pakistan, the property registration process is crucial for guaranteeing your ownership rights and avoiding legal issues. You may confidently manage the process and secure your real estate investment by Complete Guide on Property Registration Process and following the legal criteria. Buyers and sellers can confidently travel the property registry procedure and ensure a secure and transparent real estate transaction by following thorough due diligence, engaging with respected specialists, and checking the authenticity of papers.
 
Understanding the complexities of property registration not only safeguards your investment but also provides peace of mind knowing that your rights are protected under the law. Additionally, consulting with legal experts can provide valuable insights into any potential hazards and ensure a smooth transaction process. Furthermore, staying updated on any changes or amendments to property laws and regulations can help navigate the registration process more effectively and prevent any unexpected complications. Taking these proactive measures ensures a seamless property registration experience and strengthens your ownership rights in Pakistan's real estate market.
 

FAQs

1. What documents are required for property registration?

You'll need proof of identity, proof of address, sale deed, property tax receipts, and NOC from relevant authorities.
 

2. In Pakistan, how can I register my property online?

To register your property online, go to the appropriate platform, create an account, enter property information, upload necessary documents, pay fees online, and submit.
 

3. What is the Pakistani House Registry?

Registration is the formal documentation of property ownership in the owner's name. In contrast, the transfer involves the transfer of property ownership from one person to another.
 

4. What is the land registration procedure in Punjab?

Visit NGDRS (National Generic Document Registration System) Punjab for property registration. Pay the stamp duty and make an appointment with the local sub-registrar's office.
 

5. What taxes are associated with property registration in Pakistan?

Stamp duty, capital value tax, and withholding tax are all taxes involved in property registration in Pakistan.

posts.title: Step by Step Guide On How To Sell a Property In Pakistan
posts.excerpt: Selling a home in Pakistan can be one of the most complicated and difficult processes in the real estate industry. Despite the country's expanding real estate market, a number of factors can make it difficult for propert...
posts.content:
Selling a home in Pakistan can be one of the most complicated and difficult processes in the real estate industry. Despite the country's expanding real estate market, a number of factors can make it difficult for property owners to sell their properties quickly and easily. The lack of transparency and regulation in the real estate industry is one of the most significant challenges that property owners face when attempting to sell their properties in Pakistan. The high taxes and fees associated with the process can also make selling property in Pakistan difficult. While selling property in Pakistan can be a complicated and difficult process, there are steps property owners can take to make the process easier.
 
You can increase your chances of finding a buyer and getting a fair price for your property by working with an authorized property dealer, properly preparing your property for sale, and being patient and persistent. This blog will provide Step by Step Guide On How To Sell a Property In Pakistan. We will walk you through each step of the process, from market research and preparation to marketing and negotiation providing you with valuable insights and practical tips to sell your property. In this blog we’ll discuss about 
 
  • What exactly is a property transfer 
  • What exactly is a moveable property
  • Instruction to sell a property in Pakistan
  • Recognize the worth of your property
  • Prepare the property of sale
  • List the property for sale 
  • Token/Bayana
  • Commission for the agent
  • Respond to buyer inquiries
  • Negotiate with possible purchasers
  • NDC
  • Complete the sale 
  • Transfer property possession 
  • Who has the authority to transfer the property 
  • Selling and transfer of property in Pakistan 
  • Required documents 
 

What Exactly Is a Property Transfer?

Once a property has been purchased, it must be registered in the buyer's name. In legal terms, property transfer refers to a person who owns the property and has a title to it. In Pakistan, the transfer could be understood as a title transfer from one entity to another.
   

What Exactly Is Movable Property?

An immovable property is one that cannot be moved without changing its nature. It has been secured to the ground. Plots, houses, apartments, shops, and buildings or structures are examples of this type. These are all immovable and are classified as immovable properties.
   

Instructions to Sell a Property In Pakistan:

Selling a property in Pakistan can be a difficult and time-consuming process, but it can be done smoothly and efficiently with the right approach and guidance. With proper research and assistance from experienced real estate professionals, navigating through the complexities of the market and legal procedures becomes manageable, ensuring a successful sale and a satisfying experience for all parties involved.
   

Recognize the Worth of Your Property:

You must first determine the value of your property before you can sell it. A property's value can be affected by a number of factors, including its location, size, condition, and amenities. Consult a real estate agent, get a property appraisal, or research the prices of similar properties in your area to get an estimate of your property's value.
   

Prepare the Property for Sale: 

Once you've determined the value of your property, you must prepare it for sale. Cleaning and organizing the property, making any necessary repairs or renovations, and staging the property to make it more appealing to potential buyers are all examples of this. You might also think about hiring a professional photographer to take high-quality photos of your property, which could help you attract more buyers.
   

List the Property for Sale:

When your property is ready to sell, you must put it on the market. Working with a real estate agent, listing it on online property portals, or advertising it through word of mouth are all options. Additionally, you can consider staging an open house to attract potential buyers and showcase the features of your property.
   

Token / Bayana: 

In some real estate transactions, buyers provide a "Bayana" amount of money to demonstrate their commitment to the purchase. The value of the token money varies, but it is usually a small percentage of the total sale price. Before proceeding, ensure that you have a thorough understanding of the token money's terms and conditions.
   

Commission for the Agent:

Agents usually work on a commission basis, usually around 1%. They may agree to change the commission based on how quickly a deal is closed, but this is uncommon. Typically, the commission is paid when the full payment for the transaction is received.
   

Respond to Buyer Inquiries: 

As prospective buyers express interest in your property, you must respond to their inquiries and schedule showings. This can include answering property-related questions, providing additional information or documentation, and arranging for potential buyers to visit the property in person.
   

Negotiate with Possible Purchasers:

Once you've found a potential buyer for your property, you'll need to negotiate a price and other terms of the sale with them. This may require multiple rounds of negotiations and the willingness to compromise in order to reach an agreement that is satisfactory to both parties.
   

NDC Stands for No-Demand Certificate:

It is critical to apply for the No-Demand Certificate (NDC) well before the final payment date in Pakistan in order to proceed with the property sale. The transfer of property cannot take place without this certificate. Depending on where the property is located, you can obtain the NDC from the private housing society's office or the city's land development authority. The NDC declares that no taxes are owed and includes tax information for both the buyer and seller, as well as information on the transfer fee and stamp duty.
   

Complete the Sale:

You must finalize the transaction once you have agreed on the terms of the sale with the authorized dealer. This may entail completing any required paperwork or documentation, obtaining any necessary permits or approvals, and transferring ownership of the property to the buyer.
   

Transfer Property Possession: 

Once the sale is completed, you must transfer property possession to the buyer. This may involve coordinating with them to arrange for the transfer of keys, as well as ensuring that the property is left in good condition and free of personal belongings or debris.
   

Who Has the Authority to Transfer Property?

In Pakistan, only the person who owns the property and has the authority to sign the contract can transfer it. A contract connects the parties selling and buying a property. There are several types of people who cannot participate in the transfer of property, including:
 
  • A minor is someone under 18. 
  • A person who is mentally disabled
  • A person who is legally prohibited from participating in or executing any property transfer.
  • A person not in their senses
  • To transfer property to another person, a person must be at least 18 years old and in good health. A contract is signed between two parties under the Act of 1872, and the transfer of ownership has consequences on both parties.
   

Selling and Transfer of Property In Pakistan:

Selling and transferring property in Pakistan involves a meticulous process of drafting sale deeds, obtaining necessary certificates, and registering the transaction at the local sub-registrar office. Legal compliance and professional guidance are essential for a seamless property transfer experience in Pakistan. The procedure for selling and transferring property in Pakistan is as follows:
 
Agreement:
When the initial talks are completed, the parties sign a Byanya, which is a written agreement. The agreement includes the following rules:
  • The full description of the property
  • The terms and circumstances of the selling of the property
  • The total amount reached by both parties
  • The date by which the buyer is obligated to pay the remaining amount after Byanya and token
   

Documents Required for Selling OR Transferring Property In Pakistan:

The importance of having all the necessary documents required for selling a property cannot be overstated. These documents serve as legal proof of ownership, ensuring transparency and safeguarding against disputes during the transaction process. The following documents are required for the sale or transfer of property in Pakistan:
 
Recent passport-size photographs of both parties, including the buyer and seller, are required.
  • Original and valid CNIC copies
  • The seller's original title deed. The title deed is the paperwork that proves ownership to the seller.
  • The sale deed is a contract signed by the buyer and seller that is regarded as the most important property document in the country.
   

Documents Needed for the Transfer Process:

The following documents are required for the transfer process:
 
  • The Fard-e-Milkiyat (Record of Rights) is also known as the 'Fard'. This form can be obtained from the property registration office by the seller. It is a sort of guarantee from the competent authority that the seller owns this property.
  • A Non-Demand Certificate (NDC) is another important document that shows you are not responsible for any fees on the Property. This can be received from your local development authority office.
  • If you are interested in a property within a private residential housing society, you will usually need a letter from the security to complete the transfer. This could also serve as a Fard document.
  • Obtaining Stamp Paper and Making Tax Payments:
  • While purchasing the property, the buyer must also submit the following property taxes:
  • Stamp Duty of 3%
  • Capital Gains Tax of 2%
 

Conclusion:

In conclusion, navigating the real estate market in Pakistan poses numerous challenges for property owners due to a lack of transparency, high taxes, and complex regulations. However, despite these obstacles, there are strategies to facilitate the selling process. To optimize your chances of securing a favorable deal, property owners can benefit from partnering with authorized property dealers like Etihad Marketing. By partnering with authorized property dealers, adequately preparing their properties for sale, and demonstrating patience and persistence, property owners can enhance their chances of securing a favorable deal.
 
The Step by Step Guide On How To Sell a Property In Pakistan outlined in this blog offers invaluable insights, covering crucial aspects such as market research, property preparation, marketing strategies, and negotiation techniques. Understanding the details of property transfer, recognizing the value of one's property, and ensuring compliance with legal requirements are essential for a successful sale. Ultimately, by leveraging the resources and advice provided in this guide, property owners can navigate the complexities of selling a property in Pakistan with confidence and efficiency.
   

FAQs 

 

1. How is Pakistan's real estate market doing?

To summarize, the Pakistani real estate market is experiencing significant growth and development as a result of customer preferences for property investment, rising demand for housing in urban areas with gated communities, and the prevalence of informal transactions.
   

2. What are Pakistan's property transfer laws?

The Transfer of Property Act, 1882, is the fundamental law governing property transfer in Pakistan. 
   

3. In Pakistan, what is a sale deed?

A sale deed is a title document in a sale transaction that is detailed, solemn, and technical, and parties typically have it prepared, executed, and registered with professional legal advice.
